questions.prompt: In the final 60 days, who pays less for the same TV spot?
questions.why: Stations must sell candidates airtime at the lowest unit charge. Outside groups pay market rates, which climb near Election Day.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $5.1M in IA's 3rd District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is offense.

questions.prompt: FREEDOM CAUCUS FUND (a super PAC) has spent $757K in NV's 2nd District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $253K in NV's 1st District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is offense.

questions.prompt: In CO's 8th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $1.1M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $1.7M.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
How often do House and Senate campaigns file their regular reports in an election year?
questions.why: Candidate committees file quarterly, plus 12 days before and 30 days after each election. Monthly filing is only an option for PACs and parties.

questions.prompt: Does a 501(c)(4) nonprofit that runs election ads have to disclose its donors?
questions.why: It must report the ad spending, but generally not its donors unless they gave for that ad. That's why it's called dark money.
